Vaccine Science Rollout

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
While Covid deaths are continuing to rise, South Africans have a lack of confidence in Covid-19 Vaccines..

Unique Selling Point:
It's been 4 months and about 15 million jabs since the Government started vaccinating citizens.... and although the Government is making headway in vaccinating the adult population, it has not been an easy road. Masses of false information circulating on social media coupled with mistakes during the rollout have all contributed to a lack in vaccine confidence. And it's difficult to discern what is fake and what is not...

Summary:
Millions of ordinary citizens are scared to be vaccinated. They do not necessarily share the beliefs of Anti-vaxx Conspiracy Theorists, but they conflicted about the masses of information available and are questioning the efficacy of the vaccines. Those who have had Covid, believe that their natural immunity will be enough to protect them in future. Some question the ingredients of the vaccine, or the testing and trial processes that were followed. On top of all these fears, it is very difficult to understand and access the real truth. People's research seems to be headline-based and statements are often taken out of context. And the issue is driven by emotions, because we're all scared... The HSRC reports that very little vaccine hesitancy is as a result of religious beliefs, the bulk of objector are simply unsure of the science and the motivations behind mass vaccine rollouts -- The truth is that there were no deaths or hospitalisations during the Covid vaccine trials. The process was fast-tracked to minimise deaths. Vaccines save lives.

Further information:
People don't necessarily understand the science behind the vaccines, the differences between the various approved jabs, and the benefits they present. Different vaccines are linked to different efficacy percentages which is driving people's lack of confidence... A quick search on the internet says that Pfizer gives you 95% protection, Moderna 90%, Johnson&Johnson is 72% effective and AstraZeneca about 72%... but this gives you no REAL information, and without understanding the context and the "fine print" so to speak, people cannot make informed decisions with confidence.

While the Covid-19 vaccines are relatively new, the science behind them are not. Non-live vaccines have been used for decades and have proven to have no side-effects, eg. rabies, polio, Hepatitis A. The Covid Vaccine leaves your body within 72 hours. Your body makes anti-bodies to protect you against the disease. Serious side effects from the vaccine are extremely rare. You are far more likely to get long-term effects from infection that from Vaccination.

The Centre for Social Change, University of Johannesburg (UJ) in collaboration with the Developmental, Ethical and Capable State research division of the Human Sciences Research Council (HSRC) has recently released a report unpacking some of the latest findings about vaccine acceptance and hesitancy in South Africa. Although general vaccine acceptance has improved from 67% to 72%, there are still challenges. Younger people are less likely to be accepting of vaccines than older people. Vaccine acceptance declined amongst White adults from 56% to 52%, while it increased from 69% to 75% for Black African adults. However, White adults were more likely than Black Africans to have been vaccinated (16% compared to 10%).

Besides the issues of lack of trust in the Government and "Big Pharma"... there are other logistical obstacles to getting people vaccinated. Access to vaccines is still an issue that the Department is grappling with. Millions of undocumented people still need to be accommodated, should children be vaccinated and the logistics of vaccine passports needs to be worked out. On top of that Government is sticking to the "official" Covid Death numbers that massively underplays the country's problem with Covid... This adds to the "it's just a Flu" rhetoric. The sooner Government admits that we have a real crisis, the more seriously people will take the pandemic. Covid is said to be 8 to 10 times more harmful than the flu, but with a vaccine it becomes less harmful than the flu.

Experts agree that Herd Immunity is no longer attainable, especially not naturally... even if 80% of South Africans have had Covid, as Discovery has claimed.

Expert:
Dr. Nicholas Crisp
Prof. Narnia Bohler Muller
Prof. Penny Moore Senior Scientist: NICD

Press Release:


Vaccine Confidence
Widespread internet access means information at our fingertips and research shows South Africans are using multiple online sources to inform themselves on COVID-19 vaccines. But in an era of weaponised digital propaganda, disinformation is taking a toll on those people who need clear, reliable, factual information to empower informed choices. While the number of adults opting to get jabbed in South Africa has risen from 67 percent in January to 72 percent in July, it leaves just under a third of people still unable or unwilling to trust the science that vaccines are safe and effective. Carte Blanche examines how the burden of COVID-19 shifts to the unvaccinated as the jab keeps more people out of hospital and off ventilators.
Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Researcher: Laura Byrne | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


Vaccine Science Rollout FINAL SCRIPT


V/O
The South African Covid-19 vaccinometer is steadily ticking over.

So far over 15 million jabs have been administered, and about 28% of the adult population has been fully vaccinated.
UPSOUND




But realising that we have a long way to go, Government and the scientific community at large have been encouraging citizens to get vaccinated.
UPSOUND
“It will be quick now-now”
“Dankie, ne”
V/O
And the drive to push vaccinations means that you can now even be jabbed drive-through style!
LINK
It’s been over 18 months since the start of the pandemic, and many of us are still scared. Confused by masses of information from all corners, now even worse since the rollout of the vaccine programme. But how does one know what is fact and what not … Well, I thought who better to ask than the man in charge of the country’s vaccination plan...
Dr Nicholas Crisp
I’m Nicholas Crisp, I’m the Deputy Director general responsible for National Health Insurance in the National Department of Health.
V/O
Dr Nicholas Crisp is a very busy man. In addition to overseeing the NHI, he’s running the Covid Vaccine Programme, and serving as Acting Director General of Health in the absence of Dr Sandile Buthelezi.
Dr Nicholas Crisp
Masa: You have arguably one of the toughest jobs in this country right now. Tell me about some of those challenges and how it's been for you.
Well, it has been tough, but there's a remarkable team that you don't see because everybody gets to see me. A huge number of very competent people working in the background.
V/O
Having given up semi-retirement for the challenge of setting up an equitable health system for all South Africans, he now spends his days running from meeting to meeting -- with a liberal serving of press briefings in-between.


We would like to vaccinate 70 percent of the adult population by Christmas. That is our mantra that we are chasing.
V/O
And the reason for that, he says, is not just to protect individuals, but to safeguard the integrity of the entire health system.
Dr Nicholas Crisp
If every hospital is full of people needing ICU just for COVID related illness, then we don't have that capacity available for looking after people with other conditions. Currently, the capacity of the combined resources of the public and private sector is we can vaccinate at over 300000 vaccines a day. Now, we need people to come so that we can vaccinate them.
V/O
But research shows that many South Africans are still reluctant to be vaccinated against Covid-19.
Prof. Narnia Bohler-Muller
The youth are the ones who are the most hesitant...
V/O
Professor Narnia Bohler-Muller from the Human Sciences Research Council has been driving ongoing research about vaccine acceptance and hesitancy in South Africa. In January 67% of adults were willing to take the vaccine. This figure went up to 72% in July.
Prof. Narnia Bohler-Muller
What was interesting was the more educated people are, the more likely they are to be hesitant. I think educated people have access to the internet, social media - a lot more access to information, and maybe even disinformation.
V/O
According to the UJ-HSRC survey, vaccine hesitancy is driven by a general distrust in Government, and questions around the safety and efficiency of the vaccines.
Prof. Narnia Bohler-Muller
It’s very clear that the people want information. They want as much information as they can get. And so, we need to do that so that they feel comfortable about this.
LINK
Meet SARS-CoV-2 – or rather my budget-interpretation of the virus. It's a spherical membrane with the virus' genetic material on the inside. On the outside it is covered in protein spikes which it uses to attach to human cells....
V/O

Once inside, it commandeers the cell’s machinery to make bulk copies of itself…. Making you sick … and using you to transmit some of these copies to the next unprotected human.
V/O
The vaccines essentially trick your body into temporarily making the spike proteins, which are then recognised by your immune system, causing it to make antibodies and an army of T cells and memory cells to fight off future infections.
Prof Penny Moore
The Johnson and Johnson vaccine essentially takes a harmless virus called an adenovirus and uses that as a means of transporting the code for the spike protein...
V/O
While the J&J vaccine uses an inert messenger virus, the Pfizer vaccine works differently, explains Associate Professor Penny Moore from the National Institute for Communicable Diseases.
Prof Penny Moore
Here we have a mRNA molecule, which is just a different way of coding for the spike protein. And it's sort of wrapped up in a little parcel of lipids or fats to protect it.
V/O
In both cases you have no chance of contracting Covid-19 from the vaccine because you’re not actually injected with the SARS-CoV-2 virus...
Prof Penny Moore
Masa: Prof, are Covid Vaccines safe?
Yes, the simple answer is that they are safe. They have been tested in thousands and thousands of people, and there were no shortcuts taken in the development of these vaccines.
V/O
In some cases clinical trials ran concurrently, but the safety was never compromised, says Prof Moore. And most importantly, the vaccines were not developed in isolation...
Prof Penny Moore
People have the impression and it's mistakenly people have the impression that these vaccines were developed incredibly fast and that these are very new technologies. And that's that's not correct. Both for the RNA platforms and for the adenoviral platforms, the Johnson and Johnson platforms, they both come out of really decades of research that happened to mature at exactly the right time


Dr Nicholas Crisp
Masa: We have certain pockets of the community that's really skeptical and they just want to know how safe is this?
Well, so let's try and put it in perspective. No doctor will tell you that a medicine is 100 percent safe because we react differently but no medicine is given to you in a circumstance where it is not safe.
V/O
While some people are worried about possible side-effects, Prof Moore says common reactions are not a sign that vaccines are unsafe.
Prof Penny Moore
Almost everybody who receives the vaccine for SARS-CoV-2 may have a headache, may have a slightly sore arm. And in a way, you can view that as a sense that your immune system is reacting to the vaccine. That's what you wanted to do. There are occasionally very, very rare, more serious side effects...
V/O
Some complications, including inflammation of the heart muscle and blood clots, have been linked to Covid vaccines, but the experts agree that these are extremely uncommon.
Dr Nicholas Crisp
The last I saw was 58 deaths have been reported that are associated with vaccination. Now to put that in perspective of 13 million doses of vaccines that are given compared with how many deaths have we had now in the country? Hundreds of thousands, maybe, if you look at the excess deaths. This is a very small number...
V/O
Further investigation has revealed that so far these “reported associated deaths”, were not as a direct result of the Covid Vaccines, says Crisp.
Dr Nicholas Crisp
Masa: So just to be clear these 58 deaths were not caused by the vaccine?
So half are still an investigation and we'll see whether any of them were caused by the vaccine. But the other half, not one of them is caused by the vaccine.
Masa: What do you say to those who say, look, I've already had Covid, I think I've got natural immunity. I don't need to get vaccinated?
Yeah, well, for now, that might be true for the first couple of weeks after Covid. But how do you know when your immunity is going to wane? There are too many unknowns. And what we can talk about is the evidence we do not see properly vaccinated, fully vaccinated people clogging up our ICUs.
V/O
While fear and distrust are keeping people away from vaccination sites, the Covid-19 democracy Study has also highlighted the issue of access to vaccines...
Prof Bohler-Muller
Clearly there were issues around transport, around people living in remote areas and so on. So Limpopo started this drive to go out into remote rural areas and get people vaccinated and now that’s happening in other provinces as well.
V/O
And according to Government statistics it is clear that some provinces are faring better than others. To date, Limpopo, Eastern Cape and Western Cape have managed to vaccinate over 30% of their adult populations.
Dr Nicholas Crisp
That's really the challenge now to make sure there's not an inequitable distribution of the service, both between rural and urban, insured and uninsured, old and young...
V/O
Government is also extending vaccine access to undocumented individuals from October this year, and digital Covid Certificates are being rolled out, ... but internationally recognised Covid QR codes are still a problem for some travellers...
Dr Nicholas Crisp
The passport is a very different issue. Now, you have to have all those countries, embassies having access to our vaccination system, and that is really expensive to maintain. So we will we will get there. You will see developments. They do roll out as long as our budget holds. We will be able to make things smarter, faster, easier, better.
V/O
Science is ever-changing… yesterday’s unknowns become today’s answers as we continue to look for ways to protect ourselves from SARS-CoV-2…
Dr Nicholas Crisp
Masa: How does it make you feel when you hear a.. Vaccines or vaccine, hesitant people doubting this vaccine and you know how much work has been put into it?
Ja look I’m a doctor and I’ve seen patients reject treatment many times, and it's really distressing to have to see our clinical colleagues looking after people, ventilating them, taking them away from their families, putting tubes down their throats and doing whatever is necessary to try and save their lives when they could have saved their own life by being protected.
Masa: Dr. Crisp, how have the past few months changed your life?
I’ve learnt to live with less sleep...






PROMO 1 11”
Many people have questions when it comes to Covid-19 jabs… and who better to answer them than Dr Nicholas Crisp… the man in charge of the South African Vaccine Programme...
PROMO 2 21”
Covid-19 is becoming the pandemic of the unvaccinated. Evidence is showing that the jab is currently keeping people out of hospital, and off ventilators…
UPSOUND: Imagine the discomfort of lying in an ICU for a week, two weeks, three weeks, not being able to see your relatives and maybe dying there, ...
What is keeping South Africans away from vaccine stations?


PROMO 3 21”
About 28% of South African adults have been fully vaccinated, and experts are saying we’re already seeing the benefits.

UPSOUND: We do not see properly vaccinated, fully vaccinated people clogging up our ICUs,. But we do see unvaccinated people getting sick, really sick… many dying..

We dive deeper into science behind the Covid-19 Vaccines...

Prof Penny Moore People have the impression and it's mistakenly people have the impression that these vaccines were developed incredibly fast and that these are very new technologies. Prof Penny Moore Almost everybody who receives the vaccine for SARS-CoV-2 may have a headache, may have a slightly sore arm. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): While Covid deaths are continuing to rise, South Africans have a lack of confidence in Covid-19 Vaccines..
metadata.Unique Selling Point: It's been 4 months and about 15 million jabs since the Government started vaccinating citizens.... and although the Government is making headway in vaccinating the adult population, it has not been an easy road. Masses of false information circulating on social media coupled with mistakes during the rollout have all contributed to a lack in vaccine confidence. And it's difficult to discern what is fake and what is not...
metadata.Summary: Millions of ordinary citizens are scared to be vaccinated. They do not necessarily share the beliefs of Anti-vaxx Conspiracy Theorists, but they conflicted about the masses of information available and are questioning the efficacy of the vaccines. Those who have had Covid, believe that their natural immunity will be enough to protect them in future. Some question the ingredients of the vaccine, or the testing and trial processes that were followed. On top of all these fears, it is very difficult to understand and access the real truth. People's research seems to be headline-based and statements are often taken out of context. And the issue is driven by emotions, because we're all scared... The HSRC reports that very little vaccine hesitancy is as a result of religious beliefs, the bulk of objector are simply unsure of the science and the motivations behind mass vaccine rollouts -- The truth is that there were no deaths or hospitalisations during the Covid vaccine trials. The process was fast-tracked to minimise deaths. Vaccines save lives.
metadata.Further information: People don't necessarily understand the science behind the vaccines, the differences between the various approved jabs, and the benefits they present. Different vaccines are linked to different efficacy percentages which is driving people's lack of confidence... A quick search on the internet says that Pfizer gives you 95% protection, Moderna 90%, Johnson&Johnson is 72% effective and AstraZeneca about 72%... but this gives you no REAL information, and without understanding the context and the "fine print" so to speak, people cannot make informed decisions with confidence. While the Covid-19 vaccines are relatively new, the science behind them are not. Non-live vaccines have been used for decades and have proven to have no side-effects, eg. rabies, polio, Hepatitis A. The Covid Vaccine leaves your body within 72 hours. Your body makes anti-bodies to protect you against the disease. Serious side effects from the vaccine are extremely rare. You are far more likely to get long-term effects from infection that from Vaccination. The Centre for Social Change, University of Johannesburg (UJ) in collaboration with the Developmental, Ethical and Capable State research division of the Human Sciences Research Council (HSRC) has recently released a report unpacking some of the latest findings about vaccine acceptance and hesitancy in South Africa. Although general vaccine acceptance has improved from 67% to 72%, there are still challenges. Younger people are less likely to be accepting of vaccines than older people. Vaccine acceptance declined amongst White adults from 56% to 52%, while it increased from 69% to 75% for Black African adults. However, White adults were more likely than Black Africans to have been vaccinated (16% compared to 10%). Besides the issues of lack of trust in the Government and "Big Pharma"... there are other logistical obstacles to getting people vaccinated. Access to vaccines is still an issue that the Department is grappling with. Millions of undocumented people still need to be accommodated, should children be vaccinated and the logistics of vaccine passports needs to be worked out. On top of that Government is sticking to the "official" Covid Death numbers that massively underplays the country's problem with Covid... This adds to the "it's just a Flu" rhetoric. The sooner Government admits that we have a real crisis, the more seriously people will take the pandemic. Covid is said to be 8 to 10 times more harmful than the flu, but with a vaccine it becomes less harmful than the flu. Experts agree that Herd Immunity is no longer attainable, especially not naturally... even if 80% of South Africans have had Covid, as Discovery has claimed.
